title: Chapter 4 Problem Set: Binary Network Packet & Multi-Frame TLV Stream Parser (packet_parser.erl)
solutionExplanation: Complete TLV binary protocol engine with bit syntax parsing, record construction, tail-recursive stream aggregation with fragment preservation, and encode_frame packing.

otpDocCards.description: Single-instruction matching of network protocol frame headers and payloads.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: Executed directly in BEAM parser loop with zero buffer copies.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why does parse_tlv_stream return {partial, ParsedFrames, TrailingBytes} when the last frame is incomplete?

options.label: Because TCP is a stream protocol where packets can be fragmented; the socket worker must buffer the trailing bytes and prepend them to the next incoming packet
options.explanation: TCP delivers an unbroken stream of bytes with no guarantee of packet frame boundaries. Partial frames must be saved until subsequent TCP packets arrive.

options.label: Because the BEAM VM garbage collector requires all trailing bytes to be saved in an ETS table
options.explanation: It is a network stream framing pattern, not related to ETS or garbage collection.

options.label: Because Erlang cannot parse binaries with an odd number of bytes
options.explanation: Erlang parses binaries of any byte count or bit count without restriction.
